holderPosition.legalForm: Contingent contractual entitlement under Cayman-law token terms issued by Jurassic Finance Labs S.P., a segregated portfolio of Futarchy Governance SPC: a pro-rata share, in USDC, of the net proceeds if the skull is sold or insured as a total loss, granted by an unnamed Cayman SPV under a Linkage Deed
holderPosition.says: The holder is owed a pro-rata USDC share of the net proceeds only if the skull is sold or paid out as a total loss; the terms call the token 'not a share' and give no ownership of the skull. TRCH1 holders have no vote, no redemption and no buyback; RAWR holders decide any sale through MetaDAO futarchy with the operator's written consent, and nothing obliges anyone ever to sell.

statements.says: The terms say the issuer will not support any market in the token, but the sale multisig moved the treasury tokens into trading pools. On 8 October 2026 the multisig still had 633,512 USDC and no payment for the skull from it showed on chain (a payment made another way is still possible).

chainFacts.says: Classic SPL mint, 9 decimals; mint authority and freeze authority are none, no extensions. Nobody can mint, freeze or move TRCH1.
Supply 999,795.237621849 TRCH1. Against the 1,000,000 issued, 204.762378151 have been burned (Tokenizario counted about 202 on 8 October 2026).
Token metadata is immutable and carries no hashes of the terms, deed or reports.
One 3-of-4 Squads multisig is admin, escrow and treasury of the sale and can upgrade the sale program; it held 633,512 USDC with no payment for the skull on chain.

outside.says: RAWR holders through MetaDAO futarchy, with the operator's written consent; TRCH1 holders take no part. Nothing obliges a sale. Stays in the terms and the futarchy program.
If the structure fails, a company related to the founders may buy the skull at its appraised value. Stays in the terms.

Jurassic Finance's own launchpad sold 950,000 tokens at $0.6947 in USDC from 17 August 2026, no fee, no lockup, US persons excluded; the 660,000 USDC cap filled on 16 September from 359 contributions; 600,000 USDC is for the skull, about 60,000 USDC and 50,000 tokens go to the treasury; an unfilled cap would have refunded. Stays in the sale program.
Cayman law, confidential arbitration at CI-MAC in George Town, no class actions. Offered in the EU under MiCA's small-offer exemption, so no white paper was published.

verdict.summary: TRCH1 is classic SPL, so the reader can read it, and A/H/T plus valuations outlines the structure. The core does not fit: the holder has a contingent claim payable only on a sale or total loss, which 'issuer-obligation' hides, and the sale is decided by another token's holders, which has no typed form. The SPV, museum, appraiser and insurer are all unnamed, so none of the statements that would back the claim has a signer today.
